newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 13.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Irish government party Fine Gael is to carry out a 'mail shot' of Irish business to help finance its 750,000 Irish pounds spending on its general election campaign.

- Two of Europe's leading drinks companies, Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, caught the stock market by surprise on Monday when they agreed a 20 billion Irish pounds merger that will create the world's largest spirits group.
- Corporate adviser teams to both Avonmore and Waterford have been mandated to finally decide whether a realistic base exists for the proposed 2.5 billion Irish pounds merger.
- The Irish government will on Tuesday outline a central theme of its election campaign, with a promise to half the unemployment rate to below six percent over the next 10 years.
- UK Prime Minister Tony Blair is expected to indicate his commitment to the search for inclusive talks and political agreement with a visit to Northern Ireland later this week.
- Members of most of the Northern Ireland political parties will go to South Africa this month to learn how negotiations for a peaceful transition from one-party rule were handled.
- Avonmore Foods has thrown its merger proposal back into Waterford Foods' court.

- A new front in the election battle opened up on Monday evening as Ireland's Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn announced Irish government plans to fix a flat rate of 12.5 percent corporation tax from 2010.
